name: King of Libnah
overview: The King of Libnah was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the conquest of Canaan. Scripture does not provide information about his tribe or additional personal details. His significance is tied directly to his role as an adversary overcome by the leadership of Joshua in the fulfillment of God's promise to Israel.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Libnah' straightforwardly indicates his position as the monarch over the city of Libnah. The name is a descriptive title rather than a personal name and does not carry additional meaning beyond identifying his rule, as noted in Joshua 12:15.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships or personal connections for the King of Libnah beyond his status as one of the kings defeated by Joshua. There are no listed relatives or alliances in the biblical record.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Libnah's primary biblical significance lies in his defeat by Joshua, which marks a key moment in Israel's conquest of the Promised Land. His inclusion among the thirty-one kings conquered demonstrates the comprehensive nature of Israel's victory under God's guidance. This defeat highlights the fulfillment of God's covenant promises through Joshua's leadership.
